title: HTTP Event-Stream compatibility shim: ReadableStream + EventSource reconcile
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide a compatibility shim and server-side negotiation for clients using legacy EventSource (SSE) and modern Fetch ReadableStream consumers. Goal is to allow the same Redwood streaming endpoint to be consumed by both stacks without producing duplicate or corrupted chunks, while enabling graceful resume and checksum-verified partial rehydration after reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Single endpoint can serve both EventSource (text/event-stream) and ReadableStream (fetch + streaming response) consumers via a negotiation header (X-Stream-Consumer) without altering existing client code for common SDKs
Chunk envelope includes monotonic sequence ID (seq) and a per-chunk CRC32 checksum; server rejects malformed chunks and logs provenance metadata

Client reconnects support resume semantics: client sends Last-Seq header and server replays buffered state starting from next seq; replay includes boundary markers so function-call frames remain atomic
Backpressure-friendly framing: small-heartbeat frames separate large content frames to allow proxies to flush; SDKs should not coalesce heartbeat-only frames into application output
No regression on existing EventSource clients: existing consumers (including legacy SDKs) continue to receive the same event names and payloads
End-to-end tests (unit + integ) that simulate network interruptions, proxy buffering, and cooperative reconnects pass in CI with numeric stability thresholds (<=1% failure flakiness over 1000 runs)
Server emits debug-level stream-negotiation logs (request id, consumer type, chosen mode, buffer retention start seq) and includes a sampling metric for reconnect frequency
Documentation updated (Streaming API guide) with migration notes and example client snippets for fetch/ReadableStream resume and EventSource fallback
steps: Design negotiation: define X-Stream-Consumer values (eventsource, readable, hybrid) and expected handshake headers (Last-Seq, Resume-Token)
Define chunk envelope schema: {seq, type, payload, crc32, provenance} and mapping to SSE event names and to ReadableStream binary frames
Implement server middleware to detect consumer type and transform outgoing frames accordingly (text/event-stream encoding vs length-prefixed binary chunks)
Implement in-memory sliding replay buffer keyed per connection/route with configurable retention (default 10s or 10k tokens) and eviction policy
Add checksum verification and graceful reject path: on checksum mismatch, server issues stream-reset with human-readable reason and emits metric
Expose negotiation metrics (consumer_type_count, average_reconnects_per_minute, corrupt_chunk_rate) to console
Add SDK compatibility examples for Node fetch, browser fetch, EventSource polyfill, and Python requests with streaming
Write unit tests for framing/serialization, property-based tests for chunk reassembly, and integration tests that run through CI using the proxy emulator
comments: 2026-02-11 - Asha Patel: Kickoff notes: scoped to HTTP streaming endpoints (text/event-stream + application/octet-stream streaming). Decided to avoid protocol-level changes for hosted API customers—use negotiation headers only.

2026-02-18 - Luca Moretti: Initial framing prototype implemented. Binary chunk envelope works; EventSource encoder shim serializes 'data:' lines correctly. Noted odd behavior with Cloudflare buffering that delays heartbeat-only frames.
2026-02-23 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed prototype and asked for explicit replay retention config per route. Also requested metrics to track reconnect hot-spots for enterprise customers.
2026-02-28 - Design (Eli Chen): UX note: In Console streaming inspector, include negotiated consumer_type and last_seq shown in wire logs to help customers debug client compatibility issues.

2026-03-03 - QA (Marta Alvarez): Added integration tests simulating proxy buffering and large message chunking. Found a bug where heartbeat frames were coalesced by the proxy if content-length was included. Working on mitigation (send small chunked responses without content-length header).

2026-03-05 - Luca Moretti: Implemented server-side workaround for proxies: when serving EventSource consumers, emit 1-byte no-op payloads periodically to force chunked flushing. Integration tests added. Marking In Progress -> needs review for perf impact.
